Actual Phase 3 efficacy: 75; On the 580-patient randomized double-blind ABTECT-Maintenance exact-trial Phase 3 readout, Week-44 clinical remission occurred in 98/193 (50.8%) at 25mg and 100/195 (51.3%) at 50mg versus 20/192 (10.4%) placebo. Sponsor reports stratification-adjusted placebo differences 39.3 and 40.3 percentage points with both p<0.0001. Observed current results, not predictions.; Source: https://ir.abivax.com/node/12341/html; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34587385/; Uncertainty: The readout is issuer-reported (SEC-filed), detailed prespecified effect confidence intervals, full SAP, ascertainment, and handling of missing data are not fully independently verified. Patients were induction responders re-randomized for maintenance; this is not efficacy in all initiating patients. Cross-program comparator is contextual only.
Clinical importance and patient benefit: 75; At ABTECT-Maintenance Week 44, endoscopic remission was 41.5% (25mg) and 47.7% (50mg) versus placebo 9.9%; corticosteroid-free clinical remission was 45.1% and 47.7% versus 9.9%; sustained clinical remission among remission-at-induction subgroups was 67.1% and 65.6% versus 15.7%. All reported p<0.0001 in issuer SEC exhibit.; Source: https://ir.abivax.com/node/12341/html; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23964932/; Uncertainty: These are clinically meaningful mucosal and steroid-free measurements, but original public topline lacks complete patient-reported quality-of-life score tables, full multiplicity-adjusted confidence intervals and adjudicated missing-data analyses. Sustained remission compares selected induction remitters.
Statistical reliability: 50; ABTECT-Maintenance randomized 580 initial induction responders (placebo 192, 25mg 193, 50mg 195), reporting Week-44 clinical remission 10.4%, 50.8% and 51.3% with stratification-adjusted placebo differences 39.3 and 40.3 points, both p<0.0001; multiplicity and conservative missing-outcome scenarios are not supplied in full SEC summary.; Source: https://ir.abivax.com/node/12341/html; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34587385/; Uncertainty: Reported p-values and predeclared stratification are not substitutes for accessible final SAP, confidence intervals for all contrasts, imputation, sensitivity analyses or an independently reanalysed dataset. Applicant-controlled topline is the source, so robustness is not fully established.
Replication and durability: 50; ABTECT-Maintenance randomized 580 induction responders across 25mg, 50mg and placebo and found Week-44 clinical remission near 51% in both doses versus 10.4% placebo. Sponsor also reports sustained clinical remission among Week-8 remission subgroups 67.1% and 65.6% vs 15.7% placebo. Separate prior induction trials demonstrated consistent 50mg benefit; 25mg induction was less consistent.; Source: https://ir.abivax.com/node/12341/html; Benchmark: https://ir.abivax.com/static-files/99de1b8a-f695-4e75-a38f-9d970eb52d52; Uncertainty: Maintenance durability is measured in a selected responder population; the maintenance phase itself has no separate blinded confirmatory maintenance study in these sources. Induction and maintenance outcomes involve different populations/endpoints. Long-term 7-year extension described by sponsor is uncontrolled and not independent replication.
Safety and tolerability: 50; SEC-hosted ABTECT-Maintenance arm table (placebo n192, 25mg n193, 50mg n195): any TEAE 50.0%,58.0%,71.8%; serious TEAE 4.2%,2.6%,5.6%; study-drug discontinuations due to TEAE 6.8%,2.6%,4.6%; deaths 0 all groups. Serious/severe infection events reported 1.0%,1.0%,0.5%. Non-melanoma skin cancers 1 in placebo and 3 each in 25/50mg arms; single cases of prostate, breast and dysplasia in 50mg with attribution uncertain.; Source: https://ir.abivax.com/node/12341/html; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34587385/; Uncertainty: Dose-related increase in any TEAE (50mg 71.8% vs placebo 50%) counters a uniformly favorable safety claim. Serious event counts are small and uncommon outcomes underpowered; trial selection limits generalizability. Attribution of skin cancers and longer exposure risk not established by topline.
Equal 20% weights. Research only, not FDA probability. Exact-NCT snapshots retained in repository.

Actual Phase 3 efficacy: 50; ENERGIZE randomized 194 patients (130 mitapivat, 64 placebo). Hemoglobin response ≥1.0 g/dL from weeks 12-24 occurred in 55/130 (42.3%) mitapivat versus 1/64 (1.6%) placebo, adjusted difference 40.9 percentage points (95% CI 32.0-49.8), p<0.0001.; Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40544857/; Benchmark: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK599481/; Uncertainty: Published randomized controlled trial and CI support clear relative hemoglobin effect; 24-week primary observation, larger-term liver safety, REMS and posttrial benefit-risk cannot be assumed from this source.
Clinical importance and patient benefit: 75; Crosses a prespecified ≥1.0 g/dL hemoglobin-responder threshold with a 40.9-point treatment difference. Some patient-reported fatigue benefit also supported; assess clinical relevance and durability separately from biomarker response.; Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40544857/; Benchmark: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK599481/; Uncertainty: Published randomized controlled trial and CI support clear relative hemoglobin effect; 24-week primary observation, larger-term liver safety, REMS and posttrial benefit-risk cannot be assumed from this source.
Statistical reliability: 50; Peer-reviewed ENERGIZE randomized non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia trial: hemoglobin response 55/130 (42%) vs 1/64 (2%), adjusted absolute difference approximately 41 percentage points (95% CI 32–50), two-sided p<0.0001. 7 treatment-arm participants and 1 placebo participant stopped study treatment before week 24.; Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40544857/; Benchmark: https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/e9r1-statistical-principles-clinical-trials-addendum-estimands-and-sensitivity-analysis-clinical; Uncertainty: A well-defined binary primary endpoint and confidence interval are documented, but published abstract alone does not establish all SAP estimands, sensitivity under missing data or multiplicity for secondary fatigue/functional endpoints; one should not infer liver safety robustness from efficacy statistical strength.
Replication and durability: 50; Conference abstract O33 with exact NCT04770753: 182 entered OLE, 121 continuing mitapivat, 61 crossover; among 55 original randomized responders mean Hb response duration 17.9 (SD3.6) weeks within double-blind period versus 43.6 (SD24.2) weeks cumulatively through OLE. Seventy-two of 121 (59.5%) originally active-treated achieved an OLE Hb response and some lasted up to 93.3 weeks.; Source: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/bjh.70838; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40544857/; Uncertainty: OLE lacked placebo comparator, enrollment selected DB completers, includes post-hoc responder classification, different follow-up exposure (median 71 weeks active-active vs 44 weeks placebo-active) and potential informative dropout. Longer period is encouraging for persistence but uncertain for causal replication.
Safety and tolerability: 50; Peer-reviewed ENERGIZE randomized NTD thalassemia trial: treatment-emergent events in 107/129 (83%) mitapivat vs 50/63 (79%) placebo. Headache occurred in 29/129 (22%) versus 6/63 (10%); initial insomnia 18/129 (14%) versus 3/63 (5%); nausea 15/129 (12%) versus 5/63 (8%); no deaths. Hemoglobin responders 42% versus 2%. Seven mitapivat and one placebo participants stopped study treatment before week 24; this is not specifically an adverse-event discontinuation count.; Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40544857/; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42721980/; Uncertainty: The public abstract does not separately provide all arm-level serious-event and causality categories; the different thalassemia populations cannot be combined to claim head-to-head safety.
Equal 20% weights. Research only, not FDA probability. Exact-NCT snapshots retained in repository.

Statistical reliability: 50; Peer-reviewed ENERGIZE-T randomized transfusion-dependent thalassemia trial: transfusion reduction responders 52/171 (30%) vs 11/87 (13%), adjusted risk difference approximately 18 percentage points (95% CI 8–27), two-sided p=0.0003. 238/258 (92%) completed double-blind treatment.; Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42721980/; Benchmark: https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/e9r1-statistical-principles-clinical-trials-addendum-estimands-and-sensitivity-analysis-clinical; Uncertainty: The CI excludes 0 and controlled primary estimand is defined, but 8% did not complete and the abstract alone does not verify missing-transfusion assumptions, sensitivity stress testing, secondary multiplicity or predefined pooling across regions/genotypes. Replication and durability: 50; In peer-reviewed randomized ENERGIZE-T, 238 of 258 (92%) randomized participants completed the double-blind period. At least one qualifying 12-week transfusion-reduction response occurred in 52/171 (30%) mitapivat vs 11/87 (13%) placebo; adjusted difference 18 percentage points (95% CI 8–27), p=0.0003. Its long open-label extension continues and cannot be used as blinded durability replication.; Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42721980/; Benchmark: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ajh.70472; Uncertainty: The primary 'any 12-week window' response does not establish sustained reduction for each participant across the entire 48-week period. Longer-term observational extension participants are selected and receive no concurrent placebo; results, attrition patterns and long-horizon response trajectories remain incompletely disclosed.
Safety and tolerability: 50; Peer-reviewed ENERGIZE-T TDT thalassemia trial: AEs in 155/172 (90%) mitapivat versus 71/85 (84%) placebo; SAEs 19/172 (11%) versus 13/85 (15%), and AE-driven treatment discontinuation 10/172 (6%) versus 1/85 (1%). No deaths. Transfusion reduction response 52/171 (30%) versus 11/87 (13%), adjusted difference 17.6 percentage points.; Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42721980/; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40544857/; Uncertainty: Mismatched safety (172 vs 85) and efficacy denominators (171 vs 87) are preserved; source notes one mistakenly treated participant. Limited 48-week exposure, laboratory liver risk, and no long-term postmarketing safety.
